meta.title: 05.11.2026 Companiile care au nevoie de finantare, se corecteaza agresiv.
meta.thread_line: 6 threads · post-election rotation, not a rally · data-center moratorium fear and hyperscaler capex · oil, yields and Congress · SpaceX political-risk dip · Oracle's $20B raise · AMD, Nebius, IREN and the watchlist

snapshot: Source note: built from GrowYourWealth's pasted written daily note (no captions or video link), so figures are as the author states them.
Thesis: Nov 4 was **internal rotation, not a market drop**: S&P 500 +1.58% and Dow +3.03% while the Philadelphia Semiconductor index fell 3.1% to a six-month low.

Cause as he reads it: Democrats take Congress and Texas elects a governor pledging to halt new data centers, so **already-connected capacity turns scarce** and hyperscalers (AMZN +7.2%, MSFT +6.6%, GOOGL +4.1%) gained ~$750B in one session.

Losers were the suppliers and builders who must raise money: CRDO -9.9%, CRWV -9.5%, COHR -7.4%, MU -5.6%, IREN ~-11%, NBIS -6.69%; the market is splitting cash-rich buyers of AI from borrowers who build it.
Oil and yields helped: Brent -8.6% to $94.70, US10Y 4.89% (-6bp), VIX -20%; no Iran deal is announced, so he builds nothing on a quick resolution.
His plan: wait, no buying in the first hours after an extreme move, then resume; focus on SPCX and ORCL, and rebuy the 500 AMD shares he sold at $630 only **below $430**.
Warning to followers: selling AI stocks at the lowest multiples in years to buy consumer stocks at record highs is, in his words, the biggest possible mistake.
Catalysts: jobless claims today 15:30 Romania time (~197,000 consensus) and October NFP tomorrow Nov 6 (~65,000 jobs, 4.2% unemployment).

themes.title: Broad rally, narrow AI: the first post-election session splits growth in two
themes.lead: The author calls Nov 4 a rotation, with a broad risk-on tape sitting on top of a semiconductor sell-off, and says continuity, not the index color, is the test.
bullets: 9 of 11 S&P sectors rose: consumer discretionary first at +4.3%, energy last at -4.8% as oil collapsed.
Philadelphia Semiconductor fell 3.1% to a six-month low, opposite to the broad market; the Nasdaq swung nearly 5% within 12 hours.
If the S&P keeps rising while semis and AI infrastructure stay under pressure, that is sector rotation, not a recovery of the whole AI theme.

Scenarios: positive (S&P holds, yields stable or lower, AMD stabilizes, SPCX back above $140, less pressure on NBIS and IREN); base case positive market with sector rotation toward profitable, cash-rich companies; negative (yields up, budget gridlock or tighter AI-infrastructure limits) points to 7,570-7,600 on the S&P, the pre-rally zone, as a reference, not a guaranteed support.
Approach: sell nothing on one session, hold a cash reserve, avoid aggressive buying right after extreme moves, and watch each theme's weight in the portfolio.

themes.title: Data-center moratorium fear makes connected capacity scarce and rewards the hyperscalers
themes.lead: The market began pricing fewer new data centers, which lifts owners of existing capacity and hits the vendors who depend on new builds; the author says demand is intact, building capacity is what got scarce.
bullets: Trigger: Democrats take Congress and, in Texas, Hinojosa beats Abbott on a platform that includes stopping new data-center construction; he stresses they can change their mind.
Wells Fargo: Texas is **27%** of planned US capacity in gigawatts; Goldman estimates possible moratoria could affect about 45% of planned expansion.

Winners: AMZN +7.2%, MSFT +6.6%, GOOGL +4.1% (~$750B of market cap in one session). He thinks hyperscalers may cut capex over the next two quarters, which lifts free cash flow, and expects META to rebound hard alongside Google and Amazon, with Microsoft already up a lot.
Losers: CRDO -9.9%, CRWV -9.5%, COHR -7.4%, MU -5.6%; NVDA held to -1.3%; AMD erased its +9% post-earnings gain.
Hyperscaler spending is over **$740B** this year versus about $400B last year, and the market is starting to price that it will not rise further.
Demand check: Google guarantees roughly $19B of leases between TeraWulf and Anthropic for 401 MW, delivered from late 2027 to Q2 2028, signed and financed.

Some AI infrastructure trades under 10x estimated 2027 earnings; his read is the market is selling 2028 projects while 2027 projects are already launched and funded, so the dividing line is new-project dependence versus multi-year committed customers.

themes.status: BRENT -8.6% · US10Y 4.89% · DEMOCRATS WIN BOTH CHAMBERS
themes.title: Oil falls, yields ease and a Democratic Congress resets the risk, not the positions
themes.lead: Macro worked for him: cheaper oil and lower yields supported the indices, but the political result is a reason to reassess risk, not to change every position.
bullets: JD Vance said the party lost because of the war and Trump acknowledges it; the market infers the administration has reason to seek a deal with Iran, but no agreement is announced and Tehran appears to hold a hard line.
Brent -8.6% to **$94.70** in 12 hours, WTI near $88, US10Y 4.89% (-6bp), US2Y about 4.55%, VIX -20%.
Lower yields help growth valuations, but a cash-rich company benefits directly while one borrowing billions to build data centers stays exposed to financing cost; that is where the market splits.
ADP: 86,000 private jobs versus ~69,000 consensus, with a loss of 27,000 in professional and business services: moderate, not alarming, not euphoric.

Per Associated Press projections and Reuters, Democrats won the House and the Senate; the president keeps his veto, so he expects tougher budget talks and closer oversight, with possible effects on defense, AI-infrastructure regulation, energy projects and taxation over the next 3-12 months.

He is also tracking a thread on foreign election interference: under Executive Order 13848 (2018) the Director of National Intelligence must assess interference within 45 days of the election, which if confirmed fully activates the standing national emergency (sanctions, asset freezes).
Talk of blockchain-based voting infrastructure is growing; he draws no investment conclusion yet but wants it on the radar.

themes.title: SpaceX falls on political risk, which he separates from fundamental risk
themes.lead: SPCX moved opposite to the indices and he treats the dip as a discount, arguing political perception is not a proven change to contracts.
bullets: Wed close **$135.84** (-3.87%), range $133.14-140.50, volume over 135 million shares.

Reuters named SpaceX and Tesla among companies hit by the repricing of political risk, with investors weighing closer congressional oversight of Elon Musk-led companies and possible effects on government contracts and regulation.

Thesis over 5-10 years: reusable launches, Starlink, satellite infrastructure and monetizing future investment; Starlink interests him most because revenue is recurring, unlike launch, which depends on mission and contract timing.
Levels: support $133-134; resistance $140-141, then $142.74; a move above $140.50 is the first stabilization signal, losing $133.14 means selling pressure continues.
Competitive advantage does not remove valuation risk; he does not invalidate the thesis over one red session but watches contracts, regulation and above all position weight.
TSLA lost about 3.3% on the same oversight risk; his long-term Tesla thesis rests on autonomy, energy, robotics and auto profitability.

themes.title: Oracle's $20B raise: dilution and debt cost now, cash flow is the real test
themes.lead: The author's second focus after SpaceX, buying in tranches, but only cash-flow conversion of contracts, not backlog growth, will tell him if the build pays off.
bullets: Wed close **$123.73** (-1.95%), range $121.78-129.85, volume about 112 million shares; market cap about $386B and trailing P/E about 19-20.
Financing of about $20B: roughly $10B equity (86.2 million shares at $116) and roughly $10B bonds; effects are dilution and interest obligations that operations must cover.
Demand for compute is real; the issue is construction economics and the gap between contracted, recognized and actually collected revenue; a multi-year contract is not cash for funding capex today.
P/E misses lease commitments and future investment, so a proper view uses enterprise value, net debt, lease obligations and free cash flow.
Levels: first support $121-122, second $118.43, issue price $116 (a financial marker, not a guaranteed technical support), resistance $128-130.
Decisive metric for him: conversion of the contract portfolio into revenue, operating profit and free cash flow.

themes.title: AMD patience below $430, Nebius and IREN as warnings, and a shared-risk portfolio view
themes.lead: A strong AMD print is not enough for him to rebuy shares he sold at $630, and the Nebius and IREN falls on an up day show the market now sorts AI buyers from AI builders.
bullets: AMD Wed close **$488.82** (+1.02%), range $476.50-514.61; Q3 revenue about $13.4B (+45% y/y), data center about $8.5B (+97%), Q4 estimate about $17B.
Reuters: deals with OpenAI and Meta caused a non-cash charge of about $1.07B tied to share-purchase rights granted to customers, which can dilute shareholders if exercised.
Technically the $514.61 high versus $488.82 close shows much of the early gain was sold; support $476-480, resistance near $500.
He sold 500 AMD shares at $630 and will try to rebuy only below **$430**, gradually, with no regret if it never gets there.
NBIS closed **$141.49** (-6.69%), range $140.02-152.88, support near $140, resistance $150-153; IREN lost about 11%, among the worst AI-infrastructure corrections.
He does not read these as fundamental damage but will check in coming weeks whether political and financing risk changes build schedules, contracts or cost of capital.

Rest of the book: AVGO (custom AI accelerators, networking; watch hyperscaler orders, margins, cash flow), PLTR, SOFI, HOOD, RKLB (Neutron, future Congress budgets), ASTS (launches, approvals), ONDS (drones), LEU (fuel capacity, government contract timing).
Risk is cumulative: AMD, AVGO, ORCL, NBIS and IREN can all be hit by an AI-capex slowdown, as SPCX, RKLB and ASTS can by a shift in space-sector perception.

takeaways.title: Read a green index day alongside the semiconductor index before judging your portfolio; a broad rally with SOX -3.1% is rotation, not a drop.
Sort AI holdings into cash-rich buyers and borrowers who must finance builds; the market is already pricing the two differently.
Judge Oracle on conversion of contracts into revenue, operating profit and free cash flow, not backlog size.
Set a price to rebuy and let the market come to it; his level is below $430, none above.
Watch jobless claims (Nov 5) and NFP (Nov 6, ~65,000 expected): hot raises yields, soft eases rate pressure, very weak raises growth worries.
Size positions by shared exposure (AI capex, space perception), not name by name.
